ruling.recommended_action: Send the full file to a human safety reviewer: summarise the 17:09 exit request [F3] and the 17:10 reply [F4], the driver's post-trip explanation [F6], the intact GPS record showing no deviation [F1][F2], and the two clean profiles [F7][F8]; no refund or fee action, no account flag on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is filed as a safety complaint and the only contested element is whether the driver's message [F4] is intimidation or a safety instruction; the trace settles that SAFE-1 applies and that the only permitted outcome is escalate. I read the whole chat record — two messages, both timestamped [F3][F4][F5] — plus the driver's statement [F6] and the complaint. [F4] is a conditional statement of confinement issued one minute after a clear request to get out [F3]; under SAFE-1 (Ryde bars "Assault, harassment, or abuse of any kind … Threats and Intimidation"), that reading is available on the words themselves, and the driver's later assertion that it was "for her own safety" [F6] does not rewrite the contemporaneous message. Weighing the other way: the driver's statement offers a benign reading — the rider trying to open a door at the lights [F6] — and no act of locking, no door-lock log and no message after F4 appears anywhere in the record [F5], so the sentence stands alone. That is a semantic judgement about intent and context which SAFE-1 reserves to a human, so I do not decide it and I do not issue a monetary ruling. On the safety screen as a whole, there is no allegation of a traffic accident, injury or dangerous driving in the chat, complaint or statement, so SAFE-2 is not triggered; the conduct alleged is aimed at the passenger and falls under SAFE-1, which is why the screen records "suspected" rather than "none" — I read the words in context and the pair [F3][F4] is at least a hostile confinement threat, not mere rudeness in a route argument.

No fare or route limb exists. The GPS puts the actual distance 0.1 km below optimal [F1] and duration 1.9 min over estimate [F2]; there is no "Off-route segment" fact in the file, so no segment falls to be tested under RD-1/RD-2 and the segment_findings list is empty, consistent with both advocates' concession that the fixed $32.86 RydeX fare stands untouched. Because no segment counts and no clause awards anything, the amount is null and no refund, waiver or fee action is available under RD-2 or FARE-1. The profile facts [F7][F8] are recorded but decide nothing alone, and RD-6's added account flag requires an upheld route dispute in the prior 90 days, which the driver's profile shows as zero [F8] — so no flag_account on this record; whether the reviewer, seeing the verbatim message, thinks a conduct review is warranted is precisely what escalation leaves to them.

Evidence is sufficient for what I am asked to do: the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F5], the GPS record is intact and shows no deviation [F1][F2], and the driver's statement is on file [F6]. Every element my outcome needs — the words, their timing, and the absence of any route or fare defect — is settled by the record, so evidence_gap is null; the residual doubt is about meaning, not missing evidence, and it is routed to a person under SAFE-1 as the trace requires.
ruling.escalation_reason: SAFE-1 safety incident: disputed whether the driver's reply [F4] — "Sit down or I lock the doors", sent one minute after the rider's request to get out [F3] — is intimidation or a safety instruction; the driver's contrary explanation is his own post-trip statement [F6], and no act, door-lock record or later message exists [F5]. A human must read the words and intent. No route deviation [F1][F2] and no fare facts, so no monetary remedy and no RD-6 flag [F8].

rejected_claims.reason: The words and timing are accepted (F3 17:09 request to exit; F4 17:10 reply), but the cited clause SAFE-1 reserves the semantic judgement of whether that sentence is a threat of confinement to a human reader, and the driver's statement F6 supplies a benign reading; the claim cannot ground an automatic finding and no ruling follows from it.

F6 is a post-trip statement by the driver and, per the record, is the very material whose weight is disputed; F6 also says the reason was the rider's safety, so it does not establish intimidation, and the route record F1 shows the ride went to the booked drop-off with no deviation, leaving the meaning of F4 to a human under SAFE-1.

Completeness of the chat record (F5) is accepted, but it does not decide the SAFE-1 reading of F4; the complete record contains two messages and no statement that the doors were locked, so it establishes a sentence, not a threat finding.

The 1.9-minute overshoot (F2) is not evidence of a continuing threat, and F1 shows the optimal-length route was driven; duration adds nothing to the disputed words F3/F4 and cannot establish an SAFE-1 finding.
Profile facts F7 are recorded but, by the procedure applied here, never decide a case alone; a clean rider profile cannot substitute for a reading of the disputed message F4 under SAFE-1.

The point that F6 cannot override the contemporaneous F4 is accepted as far as it goes, but it does not resolve whether F4 is intimidation; that reading is exactly what SAFE-1 assigns to a human, so no finding follows.
Accepted, not a claim needing rejection: F1 shows no off-route segment, so RD-1/RD-2 give no remedy; this part of the brief is consistent with the ruling.

The escalation request is granted, but the added rider-side account-review action is not supported: no off-route segment exists (F1) and no clause gives a monetary remedy, and RD-6's flag condition requires a prior upheld dispute in 90 days, which F8 shows as zero.

The driver's benign reading of F4 rests on F6, his own later statement, and cannot rewrite the contemporaneous message; the judge cannot resolve the meaning of F4 without a human, so no 'not a threat' finding is made.

Accepted in part — the record contains exactly two timestamped messages (F3, F4, F5) and no later message — but the absence of an act does not defeat a conditional-threat allegation, and the reading of F4 remains open under SAFE-1.

The route and completion points are accepted from F1 and F2, but they do not answer the SAFE-1 conduct question about F4; RD-4 concerns justified reroutes and no traffic facts exist, and SAFE-2 is not engaged because no accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation appears in the record.
The RD-6 point is accepted: F8 shows zero upheld disputes in 90 days, so no account flag follows from RD-6; but RD-6 does not bar SAFE-1 escalation, which is required by the disputed message F4.
Accepted that F6 is the driver's account and the reviewer should weigh it, but that is what the escalation does; F6 alone cannot settle whether F4 is intimidation.
